log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Incineroar leads for Intimidate and Fake Out, which blunts the physical attackers Garchomp, Dragonite, and Kingambit. Kingambit's Steel typing handles Primarina's Fairy-type attacks, and Gholdengo's special pressure covers Dragonite and Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick 3 from our team against their Garchomp, Gholdengo, Incineroar, Primarina, Dragonite, and Kingambit. Primarina's Moonblast threatens our Dragon and Dark types, so I'm weighing how that matchup affects which three to send out.

I'll go with Incineroar for Intimidate and Fake Out pressure, Kingambit for its Dark/Steel bulk and coverage against Fairy threats like Primarina, and Gholdengo as a special attacker whose Thunderbolt punishes Dragonite and other targets. That gives a solid, simple core.

decisions.thought: Incineroar lead gives Intimidate and Fake Out control against their physical Garchomp/Kingambit. Primarina and Gholdengo cover Water/Fairy and Steel/Ghost offense.

Both leads are Incineroar, and we're faster (80 vs 60 base Speed). Fake Out goes first and flinches their Incineroar, which blocks its own first-turn Fake Out or Flare Blitz this turn. That's a strong tempo start.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Both sides have Incineroar on turn 1, with ours faster at 80 speed versus their 60. I'm weighing whether they open with Fake Out or Flare Blitz against us, and how much damage Flare Blitz would deal given our Incineroar's 90 base defense and the -1 attack drop from recoil risk.

Since we're faster, our own Fake Out goes first, flinching them and preventing whatever they intended to open with. That makes Fake Out the clear choice here.

decisions.thought: Mirror Incineroar lead is decided by speed, and my 80 Speed should outrun standard bulky Incineroar. Faster Fake Out flinches them and denies their Fake Out or Parting Shot.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating turn-one Incineroar mirror match actions and speed tie risk under limited move options.

decisions.thought: Flare Blitz is resisted by the opposing Fire/Dark Incineroar, and Protect only delays. Parting Shot stacks another Attack drop on their Incineroar, lowers its Special Attack, and forces a switch, so I get tempo while my Incineroar stays in.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Both Incineroars have -1 attack, and the opponent's is Fire/Dark so Flare Blitz would only do 0.5x damage to it, making that option weak. I'm considering Parting Shot instead to drop their stats further.

decisions.thought: I outspeed the opposing Incineroar, so Parting Shot lets me lower its offenses and pivot out safely before it attacks.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing Pokémon battle options and turn order to choose between Parting Shot, Flare Blitz, Taunt, or switching.

decisions.thought: Opponent Incineroar is at -2 Attack and likely wants Parting Shot to pivot. Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks it, trapping the debuffs.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Primarina vs Gholdengo switch against debuffed Incineroar, noting Good as Gold blocks Parting Shot.

decisions.thought: Opponent Incineroar is at -2 Attack and can't touch Gholdengo with Parting Shot, so it must switch. This is a free setup turn.

Parting Shot is useless here because Good as Gold blocks status moves, so Gholdengo ignores it. Fire is super effective against Steel, so Flare Blitz is the only real damage option. Incineroar's -2 Attack hurts, but Gholdengo attacks mainly with special moves, so Incineroar can absorb them.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at -2 attack and -1 special attack, facing Gholdengo whose Good as Gold only blocks status moves, not Flare Blitz. Since Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost, Fire is super effective against the Steel typing, so Flare Blitz should still hit hard despite the attack drop.

I'm also considering Kingambit's matchup against Gholdengo's Shadow Ball, which hits Dark types for super effective damage, while Make It Rain is mostly neutral against Kingambit's Steel typing. Overall, Flare Blitz seems like the best call here given the type advantage, even with Incineroar weakened offensively.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo outspeeds Incineroar and is at +2, so Make It Rain should knock out the weakened Incineroar before it moves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating damage and type matchups to confirm Make it Rain KOs Incineroar at 71% with +2 SpA while accounting for opponent switch options.

decisions.thought: Opposing Gholdengo is at 49% and weak to Fire, so Flare Blitz should deal roughly 40-45% even with Incineroar's -2 Attack. That is likely enough to nearly finish it or set up an easy KO next turn. Parting Shot and Protect don't pressure it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo is now at 49% HP, and since it's Steel/Ghost, Incineroar's Flare Blitz hits for super effective fire damage. My earlier Flare Blitz already dealt 57%, so I'm calculating whether another hit with the current boosted stats can finish it off.

Ghost is super effective against Dark, so Shadow Ball should hit Incineroar hard too. Given the speed and damage math, Flare Blitz still seems like Incineroar's best bet even if it doesn't guarantee the KO, so I'll go with that.

decisions.thought: Incineroar fainted, so this is a forced switch. Gholdengo is the right choice: it outspeeds the opposing Gholdengo (136 vs 84 base), and Shadow Ball is 2x super effective against it. The opponent is at 55% and our Life Orb boosts Gholdengo's damage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar down, I need to switch to either Kingambit or Gholdengo. The opponent's Gholdengo is at 55% HP with Leftovers and Good as Gold, which blocks status moves but not direct damage, and their Nasty Plot boost got reset to neutral. My own Gholdengo has strong SpA with Life Orb, so I'm weighing whether Shadow Ball is effectively super-effective against their Steel/Ghost typing or just neutral.

My Gholdengo is also much faster (136 vs their 84 base speed), so switching in now and firing off Shadow Ball next turn should land a solid or potentially lethal hit before they can threaten much back, especially since their Make It Rain would only be neutral damage against my Steel/Ghost typing. That makes switching to Gholdengo the clear choice over Kingambit.

decisions.thought: We outspeed opposing Gholdengo and Shadow Ball is super effective in the mirror, while Make It Rain is resisted.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Pokemon battle damage and speed calculations to choose Shadow Ball over Make It Rain.

decisions.thought: We outspeed the opposing Gholdengo (136 vs 84), and it is at 55% HP. Shadow Ball is super effective against its Ghost typing and carries STAB and Life Orb, so it should knock it out before it moves. Make It Rain is resisted by its Steel typing.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm comparing our Gholdengo's offensive stats with Life Orb against the opposing Gholdengo, which is down to 55% health, trying to work out if Make It Rain can secure the knockout given their defensive stat.

Shadow Ball actually looks like the better pick since it hits Ghost-types for double damage while Make It Rain gets resisted as Steel-on-Steel. With our Speed advantage letting us move first, Shadow Ball should be enough to finish off their remaining HP.

decisions.thought: Opposing Gholdengo threatens Shadow Ball, and Incineroar's Dark-type resists Ghost while threatening back with Flare Blitz. Primarina would take neutral damage with no resistance.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating type matchups and abilities to choose between Primarina and Incineroar against Gholdengo.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is faster than Incineroar (136 vs 60 base Speed), so it moves first. Shadow Ball is super effective against Fire/Dark and is STAB with Life Orb and a 203 SpA, which should KO or nearly KO Incineroar. Make It Rain is resisted by Fire, so Shadow Ball is the clear choice.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the type matchup: Gholdengo's Steel-type Make It Rain against Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing, resisted by the Fire part but neutral against Dark since Steel doesn't hit Dark super effectively.

Shadow Ball is the better call since Ghost hits Dark super effectively while being neutral against Fire, making it 2x damage with STAB and Life Orb boosting Gholdengo's SpA of 203 — that should hit hard enough to seriously threaten Incineroar, so I'll go with Shadow Ball.

decisions.thought: Incineroar resists Shadow Ball and is slower, but Flare Blitz is super effective into Gholdengo's Steel typing. At 90% with Life Orb chip, Flare Blitz should secure the knockout. Switching to Primarina risks unnecessary damage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Pokemon type matchups, move priority, and speed to choose the optimal action.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo has fainted, so the only legal action is switching in Kingambit. Its Dark/Steel typing and high Attack should let it pressure the opposing Incineroar.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Gholdengo fainted, so switching to Kingambit is the only legal move.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is faster than Kingambit and Flare Blitz is super effective against its Steel typing, so it should deal massive damage or knock it out before it moves.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the type matchups here—Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave is Dark-type, which is resisted by Incineroar's own Dark typing, and Iron Head's Steel typing gets halved by Incineroar's Fire side too, so both of Kingambit's main attacks look weak into this matchup.

On the flip side, Kingambit is Dark/Steel, meaning Incineroar's Flare Blitz hits for super effective damage, so I need to weigh whether Kingambit can survive that hit and still get a useful blow in with Kowtow Cleave despite the resistance.

Considering Swords Dance to double Kowtow's damage next turn for a likely KO, but checking if Incineroar's Flare Blitz could overwhelm Kingambit first—working out that at 2x effectiveness with STAB, Flare Blitz would deal roughly 212 damage against Kingambit's 177 HP, meaning it could be a one-shot if Kingambit stays in.

But since Kingambit outpaces Incineroar, I'm comparing attacking now with Kowtow Cleave versus Sucker Punch, since Kowtow only brings Incineroar to around 47 HP while leaving Kingambit exposed to a likely KO from Flare Blitz on the return turn either way—both lines seem to cost Kingambit, so I'm leaning toward just taking the trade with Kowtow Cleave now.
